title: Automated License Plate Reader Technology Raises Concerns Over Private Sector Compliance and Government Overreach | JD Supra

agency_candidates.display_name: New York City Department of Environmental Protection PD

summary: A Seyfarth Shaw legal alert on JD Supra discusses growing legal risks around ALPR technology, highlighting the California appellate Bartholomew v. Parking Concepts decision that allows ALPR privacy claims without additional harm, the resulting wave of class actions against private ALPR users, and the California AG's suit against El Cajon over data sharing. It also notes challenges to San Jose's ALPR practices and offers compliance recommendations for businesses.

key_quotes.quote: the Court concluded that using ALPR technology without a publicly disclosed privacy policy stating when and how ALPR is collected and used violates an individual's "right to know" of the activity, which is sufficient to allege harm under the law.
the California Attorney General pursued litigation against the City of El Cajon alleging unlawful sharing of ALPR data with out-of-state and federal law enforcement agencies.

privacy organizations have asserted that the City of San Jose utilized ALPR searches to permit law enforcement officers to constantly search for and reconstruct vehicle movements without judicial authorization
